title: Meet the UK’s next prime minister: Andy Burnham is getting ready to lead
summary:
Imagine you’re about to become the captain of a huge sports team, but you haven’t picked your co-captains yet! That’s the situation for Andy Burnham, who will be the United Kingdom’s new prime minister on Monday. He’s been busy choosing his cabinet — that’s the group of top ministers who help run the country.

Burnham used to be the mayor of Greater Manchester, a big area in northern England. Now he’s the leader of the Labour Party, and he’s taking over from Keir Starmer. When reporters asked why he hadn’t announced his team yet, he said it would cause “complete chaos” to do a half-reshuffle before he’s officially in charge. Smart thinking!

So what does he want to do? In his first speech as party leader, he promised to give “hope back” to working-class communities that feel forgotten. He wants to move power away from London and give more to local regions — that’s called devolution. He also said he’ll spend a lot of “political capital” (that means using his influence and energy) to fix social care, which helps older people and those with disabilities.

Not everyone is cheering. Nigel Farage, leader of the Reform UK party, says Burnham has “no mandate” — meaning he wasn’t elected by the whole country — and wants an immediate general election. But the Liberal Democrat leader, Ed Davey, says his “door is open” to work together. Burnham says his government will be about “problem-solving rather than point-scoring.” We’ll find out who’s in his cabinet on Monday!
why_it_matters: Who leads a country affects what schools, hospitals, and parks look like, so understanding how leaders get their job helps you follow the news.

background_read: In the United Kingdom, the prime minister is usually the leader of the political party that has the most Members of Parliament (MPs).
The country does not vote directly for the prime minister; instead, voters elect their local MP, and the winning party’s leader becomes prime minister.
Andy Burnham (the mayor of Greater Manchester) became Labour Party leader and will now take over from Keir Starmer (the previous prime minister and Labour leader).
This handover happens without a new national election, which some other parties criticize.
Article_Structure: WHO: Andy Burnham, future UK prime minister, and other party leaders Nigel Farage and Ed Davey
WHAT: Burnham is picking his cabinet and promising to focus on local power and social care, while critics demand an election
WHERE: In the United Kingdom, especially London and Greater Manchester
WHY: Because the Labour Party changed its leader, and some think the new prime minister should get a direct vote from the people

perspectives.description: Burnham’s promise to share power with regions outside London could make local communities feel more listened to and get better services.
Nigel Farage argues that without a general election, Burnham’s government lacks the people’s approval and might not have a clear plan.
Ed Davey is willing to cooperate, which shows that even rival parties sometimes find common ground to solve problems.
